70ede5a1d43f0fd82b97c82c66e718a002291b62.title: Injectivity of compact Gaussian convolution
70ede5a1d43f0fd82b97c82c66e718a002291b62.body:
Let \(\sigma\in\mathbb R\), and let \(\Phi_\sigma\) denote the centered Gaussian probability measure with variance \(\sigma^2\), with \(\Phi_0=\delta_0\), the unit point mass at zero. Let \(\mu_1,\mu_2,\nu_1,\nu_2\) be nonnegative Borel measures on \(\mathbb R\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Error scale.)} \(0\le \sigma\le 1/4\).
\item \textbf{(Finiteness and support.)} Each of \(\mu_1,\mu_2,\nu_1,\nu_2\) is finite and assigns zero mass to \(\mathbb R\setminus[-1/2,1/2]\).
\item \textbf{(Convolution equality.)}
\[
\mu_1*\Phi_\sigma+\nu_2*\Phi_\sigma
=
\nu_1*\Phi_\sigma+\mu_2*\Phi_\sigma.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\mu_1+\nu_2=\nu_1+\mu_2.
\]

278609e5efacb22b389fb8a13cb7fcf8de724987.title: Weighted packet construction
278609e5efacb22b389fb8a13cb7fcf8de724987.body:
For every fixed \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), the degeneracy exponent, there exist real constants \(C>0\) and \(c>0\) such that, for every integer \(m\ge4\), the filtered-Jacobi construction has positive normalizing value:
\[
\begin{cases}
K_m(-1)>0, & \kappa>0,\\
\widetilde K_m(0)>0, & \kappa=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Here \(K_m(-1)\) and \(\widetilde K_m(0)\) are respectively the endpoint and symmetric interior normalizing values of the construction. The resulting normalized, tapered, zero-extended packet \(\psi_m\) is even and continuously differentiable on \(\mathbb R\), and satisfies
\[
\psi_m(u)=0\quad\text{for }u\notin[-1,1],
\qquad
\psi_m(0)=1,
\]
\[
|\psi_m(u)|\le C,\qquad
|\psi_m'(u)|\le Cm
\quad\text{for every }u\in\mathbb R,
\]
\[
\int_{-1}^{1}|u|^\kappa|\psi_m(u)|\,du
\le Cm^{-\kappa-1},
\qquad
\int_{-1}^{1}|u|^\kappa\psi_m(u)^2\,du
\le Cm^{-\kappa-1},
\]
and
\[
\int_{-1}^{1}|u|^\kappa u^j\psi_m(u)\,du=0
\quad\text{for every integer }0\le j<cm.
\]

67351a44ad9e5ede15a19ab7065a5e6cb2fb6765.title: Finite-sample honesty and length
67351a44ad9e5ede15a19ab7065a5e6cb2fb6765.body:
Fix \(\beta\in[1/2,1]\) and \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), and set the noncoverage probability to \(\alpha=1/10\). For any potential-outcome path space \((\mathcal S,\mathcal E)\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}, let \(\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\) be the class of structural probability laws satisfying the bounded noisy-dose model restrictions. Define the causal target by
\[
\theta(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y(a_0)],
\]
where \(a_0\) is the prespecified evaluation dose and \(Y(a_0)\) is the potential outcome at that dose. Let \(Q_P^n\) be the observed product experiment in \cref{obj:def:observed-experiment}, and let \(C_{n,\sigma}\) be the interval in \cref{obj:def:honest-interval}.

For every such path space, every integer \(n\ge0\), every \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), and every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\),
\[
Q_P^n\{\theta(P)\in C_{n,\sigma}\}\ge 1-\alpha.
\]
Moreover, there exist \(C>0\) and an integer \(n_0\ge0\), depending only on \(\beta\) and \(\kappa\), such that, simultaneously for every such path space, every \(n\ge n_0\), every \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), and every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\),
\[
\mathbb E_{Q_P^n}\!\left[\operatorname{length}(C_{n,\sigma})\right]
\le C\rho_{n,\sigma},
\qquad
\rho_{n,\sigma}=b_{n,\sigma}^{\beta},
\]
where \(b_{n,\sigma}\) is the prescribed localization scale.

68870731ef8ae8d6b06d72f581660f8eac97e88b.title: Uniform observable upper bound
68870731ef8ae8d6b06d72f581660f8eac97e88b.body:
Fix the smoothness exponent \(\beta\in[1/2,1]\) and the design-decay exponent \(\kappa\in[0,2]\). There exist a finite constant \(C>0\) and an integer \(n_0\), uniform over all public measurable potential-path spaces in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}, such that the following assertions hold for every such space, every integer \(n\ge n_0\), and every public error scale \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\).

Let \(\widehat\theta\) be the total estimator in \cref{obj:def:total-estimator}, including its empty-block fallback, and let \(Q_P^n\) be the observed experiment in \cref{obj:def:observed-experiment}. Write
\[
\theta(P)=E_P[Y(a_0)],
\qquad
L_n=\log(en),
\qquad
\rho_{n,\sigma}=b_{n,\sigma}^{\beta},
\]
where \(a_0\) is the prespecified evaluation dose and \(b_{n,\sigma}\) is the established piecewise localization scale. For every structural law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\), if the observed sample satisfies \cref{obj:ass:iid}, then
\[
E_{Q_P^n}\!\left[\,|\widehat\theta-\theta(P)|\,\right]
\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}.
\]

The dictionary in \cref{obj:def:weight-dictionary} also supplies the following comparison pairs. For each pair, \(q\) denotes its latent weight, \(\ell_q\) its observable inverse, \(A_q\) its public score, and \(V_q\) its public second-moment bound. Each supplied pair satisfies the usual measurability and integrability conditions, together with
\[
q(t)\ge0\quad\left(-\tfrac12\le t\le\tfrac12\right),
\qquad
0<I_\kappa(q):=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^\kappa q(t)\,dt<\infty,
\]
and the pointwise Gaussian inversion identity
\[
E\!\left[\ell_q(t+\sigma Z)\right]=q(t)
\quad\left(-\tfrac12\le t\le\tfrac12\right),
\qquad Z\sim N(0,1).
\]
More precisely:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Fourier comparison.)}
If \(\sigma\le L_n^{-1/2}\), there exists an integer \(k\ge0\) whose Fourier tag belongs to \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\). Its associated Fourier pair satisfies the conditions above and
\[
V_q<\infty,
\qquad A_q\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Polynomial comparison.)}
If \(L_n^{-1/2}<\sigma\), there exists an integer \(j\ge0\) whose polynomial tag belongs to \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\). Its associated polynomial pair has degree \(m=2^j+1\), satisfies the conditions above, and obeys
\[
V_q<\infty,
\qquad A_q\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}.
\]
\end{itemize}

63863051ada0dfa4e312b87ac18f52a7c77596d3.title: Jacobi polynomial binomial representation
63863051ada0dfa4e312b87ac18f52a7c77596d3.body:
Let \(a,b\in\mathbb R\) satisfy \(a,b>-1/2\), let \(j\ge0\) be an integer, and let \(z\in\mathbb R\). Write \(P_j^{(a,b)}=\mathsf J_j^{(a,b)}\) for the standard Jacobi polynomial. Define the generalized binomial coefficient, for \(v\in\mathbb R\) and integers \(i\ge0\), by
\[
\binom{v}{i}=\frac{\prod_{k=0}^{i-1}(v-k)}{i!},
\qquad \binom{v}{0}=1,
\]
where the empty product equals \(1\). Then
\[
P_j^{(a,b)}(z)
=2^{-j}\sum_{i=0}^{j}
\binom{j+a}{i}\binom{j+b}{j-i}
(z-1)^{j-i}(z+1)^i.
\]

80204999f118641708df51f708c7e5e869c25abe.title: Dictionary admissibility and score bounds
80204999f118641708df51f708c7e5e869c25abe.body:
Fix a public potential-path space as in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}, \(\beta\in[1/2,1]\), and \(\kappa\in[0,2]\). Use the finite public dictionary \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\) and its associated inverse pairs from \cref{obj:def:weight-dictionary}. Write \(A_q\) for the public expected-error score of a dictionary pair, and let \(\widehat q\) be its first score minimizer in the fixed dictionary order:
\[
\widehat q
=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{q\in\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}} A_q,
\]
with ties resolved by that order. Write \(\rho_{n,\sigma}=b_{n,\sigma}^{\beta}\) for the frontier rate, where \(b_{n,\sigma}\) is the localization scale, and set \(L_n=\log(en)\).

For every positive integer \(n\), every \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), and every pair \((q,\ell_q)\in\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\), the functions are measurable and satisfy the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive weighted moment.)} The latent weight is nonnegative on \([-1/2,1/2]\), and its design-weighted moment satisfies
\[
0<I_\kappa(q)
:=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^\kappa q(t)\,dt
<\infty.
\]
\item \textbf{(Exact Gaussian inversion.)} For a standard Gaussian integration variable \(Z\), the inverse weight is absolutely integrable at every latent displacement and satisfies
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[|\ell_q(t+\sigma Z)|\right]<\infty,
\qquad
\mathbb E\!\left[\ell_q(t+\sigma Z)\right]=q(t),
\qquad t\in[-1/2,1/2].
\]
\item \textbf{(Finite second moment.)} The extended inverse-weight second moment satisfies
\[
V_q
:=16\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^\kappa
       \mathbb E\!\left[\ell_q(t+\sigma Z)^2\right]\,dt
<\infty.
\]
\item \textbf{(Integrability under model laws.)} For every structural probability law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\), the bounded noisy-dose model class, the inverse weight is absolutely integrable under the observed centered-dose coordinate \(V\):
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[|\ell_q(V)|\right]<\infty.
\]
\end{itemize}

There exist a real constant \(C>0\) and an integer \(n_0\ge0\), independent of \(\sigma\), such that, for every integer \(n\ge n_0\) and every \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\),
\[
A_{\widehat q}\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}.
\]
Moreover, when \(\sigma\le L_n^{-1/2}\), there exists an integer \(k\ge0\) whose Fourier pair belongs to \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\) and has score at most \(C\rho_{n,\sigma}\). When \(L_n^{-1/2}<\sigma\), there exists an integer \(j\ge0\) whose polynomial pair, with index \(m=2^j+1\), belongs to \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\) and has score at most \(C\rho_{n,\sigma}\).

44b2155535abf7fe94e1f0cd83f2048132c5233f.title: Positive denominators and localization bounds
44b2155535abf7fe94e1f0cd83f2048132c5233f.body:
Let \((\mathcal S,\mathcal E)\) be a potential-path space satisfying \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}. Write \(\mathcal X=\{0,1\}\) for the two observed strata, and let \(X,A,Z,Y\) denote the stratum, latent dose, standardized error, and realized outcome coordinates of a structural law \(P\). Define the target dose, contaminated dose, and centered observed dose by
\[
a_0=\frac12,\qquad W=A+\sigma Z,\qquad V=W-a_0.
\]
Suppose the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Parameter ranges.)} The smoothness, design-decay, and error-scale parameters satisfy
\[
\beta\in[1/2,1],\qquad \kappa\in[0,2],\qquad \sigma\in[0,1/4].
\]
\item \textbf{(Structural model.)} The law satisfies \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\), as defined in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Public weight.)} The public weight \(q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is Borel measurable and nonnegative on \([-1/2,1/2]\), and its design-weighted moment satisfies
\[
I_\kappa(q)=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^\kappa q(t)\,dt,
\qquad 0<I_\kappa(q)<\infty.
\]
\item \textbf{(Gaussian inverse.)} The inverse weight \(\ell_q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is Borel measurable. For every \(t\in[-1/2,1/2]\), with expectation taken under a standard normal variable \(Z\),
\[
E_Z\!\left[|\ell_q(t+\sigma Z)|\right]<\infty,
\qquad E_Z[\ell_q(t+\sigma Z)]=q(t).
\]
\item \textbf{(Law integrability.)} The observed inverse weight satisfies
\[
E_P[|\ell_q(V)|]<\infty.
\]
\end{itemize}
Define the public denominator and localization-bias bounds by
\[
I_{\kappa+\beta}(q)
=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^{\kappa+\beta}q(t)\,dt,
\qquad
b_q=\frac{I_\kappa(q)}{16},
\qquad
B_q=64\,\frac{I_{\kappa+\beta}(q)}{I_\kappa(q)}.
\]
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the population localized ratio
\[
m_{x,q}
=\frac{E_P[\mathbf 1\{X=x\}Y\ell_q(V)]}
       {E_P[\mathbf 1\{X=x\}\ell_q(V)]}
\]
has a strictly positive denominator and satisfies
\[
0<E_P[\mathbf 1\{X=x\}\ell_q(V)],
\qquad
b_q\le E_P[\mathbf 1\{X=x\}\ell_q(V)],
\qquad
|m_{x,q}-\mu_x(a_0)|\le B_q,
\]
where \(\mu_x(a_0)\) is the conditional potential-outcome mean defined in \cref{obj:def:conditional-potential-mean}. These conclusions hold for every law and weight pair satisfying the stated conditions, including at \(\sigma=0\).

58bf40d2d5ed8a140a51d79282674b3afd3ef883.title: Identification of causal evaluation
58bf40d2d5ed8a140a51d79282674b3afd3ef883.body:
Fix the public potential-outcome path space in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}. Let \(\mathcal X=\{0,1\}\) be the two observed strata, and let \(P,P'\) be structural probability laws on
\(\mathcal X\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\times\mathcal S\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\),
whose coordinates include the stratum \(X\), latent dose \(A\), Gaussian error \(Z\), potential-outcome schedule, and realized outcome \(Y\). Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Parameter ranges.)}
\[
\beta\in[1/2,1],\qquad \kappa\in[0,2],\qquad \sigma\in[0,1/4].
\]
\item \textbf{(Model membership.)}
Both \(P\) and \(P'\) belong to \(\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Observed-law equality.)}
The two laws induce the same distribution of \((X,W,Y)\), where the contaminated dose is
\[
W=A+\sigma Z.
\]
\end{itemize}
Set the evaluation dose and centered latent dose to
\[
a_0=\frac12,\qquad t=A-a_0,
\]
and, under \(P\), write
\[
p_x=P(X=x).
\]
Use the conditional potential mean \(\mu_x(a)\) from \cref{obj:def:conditional-potential-mean}, with quantities under \(P'\) interpreted analogously.

For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the stratum probabilities, conditional laws of \(A-a_0\) given \(X=x\), and conditional potential means at every \(a\in[0,1]\) coincide under \(P\) and \(P'\). The marked latent measures also coincide: these are the measures assigning each Borel set \(B\subseteq\mathbb R\) the mass
\[
\int_B \max\{\mu_x(t+a_0),0\}\,
       P(A-a_0\in dt\mid X=x),
\]
with the corresponding expression under \(P'\).

Furthermore, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and every integer \(j\ge0\),
\[
P\!\left(
-\frac1{j+3}<A-a_0<\frac1{j+3}
\,\middle|\,X=x
\right)>0,
\]
and the shrinking-neighborhood ratios satisfy
\[
\lim_{j\to\infty}
\frac{
\displaystyle\int_{(-1/(j+3),\,1/(j+3))}
\max\{\mu_x(t+a_0),0\}\,
P(A-a_0\in dt\mid X=x)
}{
\displaystyle P\!\left(
-\frac1{j+3}<A-a_0<\frac1{j+3}
\,\middle|\,X=x
\right)
}
=\mu_x(a_0).
\]
Consequently, the population causal mean at the evaluation dose satisfies
\[
\theta(P)
=\mathbb E_P[Y(a_0)]
=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x\mu_x(a_0),
\qquad
\theta(P)=\theta(P')
=\mathbb E_{P'}[Y(a_0)].
\]

22326ed363fef64e7b6a3356e3a7c556cb4e8278.title: Uniform risk and transitions
22326ed363fef64e7b6a3356e3a7c556cb4e8278.body:
Fix the smoothness exponent \(\beta\in[1/2,1]\) and the design-decay exponent \(\kappa\in[0,2]\). Write
\[
d=2\beta+\kappa+1,\qquad L_n=\log(en),\qquad
\rho_{n,\sigma}=b_{n,\sigma}^{\beta},
\]
where \(b_{n,\sigma}\) is the localization scale in the frontier construction, and define the transition thresholds and comparison scales by
\[
a_n=n^{-1/d},\qquad b_n=L_n^{-1/2},\qquad D_n=a_n,
\]
\[
F_n(\sigma)=\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{\log(e+n\sigma^d)}},
\qquad
P_n(\sigma)=\frac{\log(e+\sigma^2L_n)}{L_n}.
\]
For each public potential-outcome path space in \(\cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}\), let \(R_n(\sigma)\) and \(H_n(\sigma)\) be the minimax expected absolute error and minimum worst-law expected connected-interval length in \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk,obj:def:honest-length}\), respectively, with noncoverage probability \(\alpha=1/10\).

There exist real constants \(0<c<C\) and an integer \(n_0\), uniform over these path spaces, such that for every such path space, every integer \(n\ge n_0\), and every \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\),
\[
c\rho_{n,\sigma}\le R_n(\sigma)\le C\rho_{n,\sigma},
\qquad
c\rho_{n,\sigma}\le H_n(\sigma)\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}.
\]
The same constant \(C\) also satisfies, for every integer \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
D_n\le C F_n(a_n),\qquad F_n(a_n)\le C D_n,
\]
\[
F_n(b_n)\le C P_n(b_n),\qquad
P_n(b_n)\le C F_n(b_n).
\]

For every real \(K\ge1\), there exist a real constant \(C_K\ge1\) and an integer \(n_K\) such that for every integer \(n\ge n_K\),
\[
0<\frac{a_n}{K},\qquad Ka_n\le\frac14,\qquad
0<\frac{b_n}{K},\qquad Kb_n\le\frac14,
\]
and simultaneously
\[
C_K^{-1}D_n\le F_n(\sigma)\le C_KD_n
\qquad
\text{for every }\sigma\in[a_n/K,Ka_n],
\]
\[
C_K^{-1}P_n(\sigma)\le F_n(\sigma)\le C_KP_n(\sigma)
\qquad
\text{for every }\sigma\in[b_n/K,Kb_n].
\]

For every fixed \(\sigma\in(0,1/4]\), there exist real constants \(0<c_\sigma<C_\sigma\) and an integer \(n_\sigma\), uniform over the public path spaces, such that for every such path space and every integer \(n\ge n_\sigma\),
\[
c_\sigma\left(\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^\beta
\le R_n(\sigma)\le
C_\sigma\left(\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^\beta,
\]
\[
c_\sigma\left(\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^\beta
\le H_n(\sigma)\le
C_\sigma\left(\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^\beta.
\]

93b64e2e4660f8e1ba632440bad11969585e7f0c.title: Realized dose conditional mean
93b64e2e4660f8e1ba632440bad11969585e7f0c.body:
Let \(\mathcal X=\{0,1\}\), and let \(X,A,Z,Y\) denote the stratum, latent dose, classical error, and realized outcome coordinates under the structural probability law \(P\), respectively. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Schedule space.)} The measurable schedule space \((\mathcal S,\mathcal E)\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}\).
\item \textbf{(Parameters.)} The smoothness parameter \(\beta\), design parameter \(\kappa\), and error scale \(\sigma\) satisfy
\[
\beta\in[1/2,1],\qquad \kappa\in[0,2],\qquad \sigma\in[0,1/4].
\]
\item \textbf{(Model.)} \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\), as defined in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\).
\end{itemize}
With \(\mu_x(a)\) the conditional potential-outcome mean defined in \(\cref{obj:def:conditional-potential-mean}\), we have
\[
0\le Y\le1\quad P\text{-almost surely},
\qquad
E_P[Y\mid A,X,Z]=\mu_X(A)\quad P\text{-almost surely},
\qquad
E_P[Y\mid A,X]=\mu_X(A)\quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
Moreover, for every bounded measurable function
\(F:\mathbb R\times\mathcal X\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\),
\[
E_P\!\left[F(A,X,Z)Y\right]
=
E_P\!\left[F(A,X,Z)\mu_X(A)\right].
\]

2ba2cb4b34e9e60a644543b0058c607a192c1e02.title: Error-free weak-design reduction
2ba2cb4b34e9e60a644543b0058c607a192c1e02.body:
Fix \(\beta\in[1/2,1]\) and \(\kappa\in[0,2]\). At error scale \(\sigma=0\), there exist constants \(0<c<C\) and an integer \(n_0\) such that, for every public measurable potential-path space as in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space} and every integer \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
c\,n^{-\beta/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}
\le R_n(0)
\le C\,n^{-\beta/(2\beta+\kappa+1)},
\qquad
c\,n^{-\beta/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}
\le H_n(0)
\le C\,n^{-\beta/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}.
\]
Here \(R_n\) is the minimax expected absolute error in \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk}, and \(H_n\) is the minimum worst-law expected connected-interval length in \cref{obj:def:honest-length}, evaluated at noncoverage probability \(\alpha=1/10\). The constants and \(n_0\) are uniform over the public potential-path space.

The risk also admits the following comparison with Gaiffas's direct Gaussian-response benchmark, specialized to smoothness \(\beta\) and design exponent \(\kappa\) \citep[Definition 2 and Theorem 1, with loss parameter one]{gaiffas2005}. Fix:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Benchmark parameters.)} Constants \(c_{\mathrm G},r_{\mathrm G},M_{\mathrm G},\tau_{\mathrm G}>0\).
\item \textbf{(Evaluation point.)} A dose \(x_*\in(0,1)\).
\item \textbf{(Design neighborhood.)} A radius \(0<\delta\le\min\{x_*,1-x_*\}\) and a design distribution on \([0,1]\) with a nonnegative measurable density \(g\) satisfying
\[
g(u)=c_{\mathrm G}|u-x_*|^\kappa
\quad\text{for every }u\in[0,1]\text{ with }|u-x_*|\le\delta.
\]
\end{itemize}
For this benchmark, the observations are
\[
B_i=f(D_i)+\xi_i,\qquad i=1,\ldots,n,
\]
where the \(D_i\) are independent draws from the fixed design distribution and the \(\xi_i\) are independent \(N(0,\tau_{\mathrm G}^2)\) errors, independent of the design. The supremum over \(f\) below ranges over Borel functions \(f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R\) satisfying
\[
\|f\|_\infty\le M_{\mathrm G},
\qquad
\inf_{p:\,\deg p\le\lfloor\beta\rfloor}
\ \sup_{\substack{u\in[0,1]\\|u-x_*|\le a}}
|f(u)-p(u-x_*)|
\le r_{\mathrm G}a^\beta
\quad
\text{for every }
0<a\le
\left\{
\frac{\tau_{\mathrm G}^2(\kappa+1)}
     {2c_{\mathrm G}r_{\mathrm G}^2n}
\right\}^{1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)},
\]
with the infimum taken over real polynomials. In particular, at \(\beta=1\) these are polynomials of degree at most one.

There exist constants \(0<c<C\) and an integer \(n_0\), depending on the fixed benchmark parameters, evaluation point, neighborhood, and design distribution, such that, for every public potential-path space and every integer \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
c\,\inf_{\widehat f}\sup_f
E_f\bigl|\widehat f(x_*)-f(x_*)\bigr|
\le R_n(0)
\le
C\,\inf_{\widehat f}\sup_f
E_f\bigl|\widehat f(x_*)-f(x_*)\bigr|.
\]
The infimum ranges over measurable estimators based on the direct observations, and \(E_f\) denotes expectation under their observed law. These comparison constants and \(n_0\) are uniform over the public potential-path space.

719e73fd24676e599306a990f8a08de53fe79840.title: Public expected-error certificate
719e73fd24676e599306a990f8a08de53fe79840.body:
Fix a public potential-outcome path space as in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}, smoothness parameter \(\beta\in[1/2,1]\), design exponent \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), sample size \(n\ge3\), and error scale \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\). Let \(P\) be a structural probability law and \((q,\ell_q)\) a public latent weight and its observable inverse. Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model.)} \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\), the model class in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} The observed sample satisfies \cref{obj:ass:iid} under \(Q_P^n\), the observed product experiment in \cref{obj:def:observed-experiment}.
\item \textbf{(Positive weight moment.)} The weights are measurable, \(q(t)\ge0\) for every \(t\in[-1/2,1/2]\), and the design-weighted moment satisfies
\[
0<I_\kappa(q):=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^\kappa q(t)\,dt<\infty.
\]
\item \textbf{(Pointwise inversion.)} For every \(t\in[-1/2,1/2]\), the inverse weight is absolutely integrable under the standard Gaussian law and satisfies
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}|\ell_q(t+\sigma z)|\,d\Phi_1(z)<\infty,
\qquad
\int_{\mathbb R}\ell_q(t+\sigma z)\,d\Phi_1(z)=q(t),
\]
where \(\Phi_1\) is the standard Gaussian probability measure.
\item \textbf{(Law integrability.)} With \(V=W-a_0\) the observed dose centered at the prespecified evaluation dose \(a_0\), absolute integrability holds under the particular structural law \(P\):
\[
E_P|\ell_q(V)|<\infty.
\]
\item \textbf{(Finite second moment.)} The extended Gaussian inverse-weight second moment is finite:
\[
V_q:=
16\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^\kappa
\left(\int_{\mathbb R}\ell_q(t+\sigma z)^2\,d\Phi_1(z)\right)\,dt
<\infty.
\]
\end{itemize}
Let \(\widehat p_x\) denote the split-sample stratum-frequency estimate and \(\widehat\mu_x(q)\) the clipped empirical stratum ratio in the established estimator construction. The corresponding estimator and population causal target are
\[
\widehat\theta_q=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat p_x\,\widehat\mu_x(q),
\qquad
\theta(P)=E_P[Y(a_0)],
\]
where \(\mathcal X\) is the set of two observed strata. Writing \(B_q\) for the public localization-bias bound and \(b_q\) for the public weighted-stratum denominator lower bound, the expected absolute error satisfies
\[
E_{Q_P^n}\bigl|\widehat\theta_q-\theta(P)\bigr|
\le
B_q+\frac{12}{b_q}\sqrt{\frac{V_q}{n}}
+2\sqrt{\frac{3}{n}}
=:A_q.
\]

6af2f6dc2e917b4eba73d6aba0c98458b2a7d188.title: Latent dose support
6af2f6dc2e917b4eba73d6aba0c98458b2a7d188.body:
The latent dose \(A\) satisfies
\[
A\in[0,1]\qquad\text{almost surely}.
\]

45d9e274e136cbec4ebc52a40157a476e4fa8cf9.title: Conditional design density bounds
45d9e274e136cbec4ebc52a40157a476e4fa8cf9.body:
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the conditional density \(g_x\) of the centered latent dose is a Lebesgue density satisfying
\[
\frac14|t|^\kappa\le g_x(t)\le16|t|^\kappa
\qquad\text{for almost every }t\in[-1/2,1/2].
\]

4c340f931920db1a312e7c6d63f1b09906026bbe.title: Standard Gaussian error law
4c340f931920db1a312e7c6d63f1b09906026bbe.body:
The standardized error coordinate \(Z\) satisfies
\[
Z\sim N(0,1).
\]

ab4e8d24def1d07b16a50181b71258c271616784.title: Classical error independence
ab4e8d24def1d07b16a50181b71258c271616784.body:
The standardized error coordinate \(Z\) is independent of the observed stratum \(X\), latent dose \(A\), and potential-outcome schedule \(Y(\cdot)\):
\[
Z\perp(X,A,Y(\cdot)).
\]

eae4ee9a7627a7f4ef26b0c2c0811923d698b225.title: Conditional uniform rank law
eae4ee9a7627a7f4ef26b0c2c0811923d698b225.body:
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the uniform-rank coordinate \(U\) satisfies
\[
U\mid X=x\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1].
\]

fc98e9f3e22927b7a5fcfdb19f07ea53166431d9.title: Conditional rank–dose independence
fc98e9f3e22927b7a5fcfdb19f07ea53166431d9.body:
The rank coordinate \(U\) and latent dose \(A\) are conditionally independent given the observed stratum \(X\):
\[
U\perp A\mid X.
\]

bf20577ddefd20916eaada682ca50e6e63b2a3e7.title: Independent and identically distributed observations
bf20577ddefd20916eaada682ca50e6e63b2a3e7.body: The observed records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), each consisting of the observed stratum, contaminated dose, and realized outcome, are independent and identically distributed under the structural law \(P\).

fc218f28331859a50db2f5fa69d90c16d5351ee4.title: Conditional potential-outcome unconfoundedness
fc218f28331859a50db2f5fa69d90c16d5351ee4.body:
The measurable random potential-outcome schedule \(Y(\cdot)\) and latent dose \(A\) are conditionally independent given the observed stratum \(X\):
\[
Y(\cdot)\perp A\mid X.
\]

696acbdf852888bd7581576de5d1fb252db53459.title: Observed experiment \(Q_P^n\)
696acbdf852888bd7581576de5d1fb252db53459.body:
The sample observed-law experiment is
\[
Q_P^n=\mathcal L_P(O_1,\ldots,O_n),
\]
where \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed observed records under the structural law \(P\), each consisting of the observed stratum, contaminated dose, and realized outcome.

9f958958c316f07c630bd7ba4752f6b14741ae17.title: Frontier rate \(\rho_{n,\sigma}\)
9f958958c316f07c630bd7ba4752f6b14741ae17.body:
The frontier rate and its localization scale are
\[
\rho_{n,\sigma}=b_{n,\sigma}^{\beta},
\qquad
b_{n,\sigma}=
\begin{cases}
n^{-1/d},&0\le\sigma\le n^{-1/d},\\[2pt]
\dfrac{\sigma}{\sqrt{\log(e+n\sigma^d)}},
&n^{-1/d}<\sigma\le L_n^{-1/2},\\[6pt]
\dfrac{\log(e+\sigma^2L_n)}{L_n},
&L_n^{-1/2}<\sigma\le1/4.
\end{cases}
\]
Here the effective exponent \(d\) and logarithmic sample-size quantity \(L_n\) are
\[
d=2\beta+\kappa+1,
\qquad
L_n=\log(en).
\]

6ae627e7b40b68a8d2dc87de0faf820e6b40f34e.title: Inverse-weight dictionary \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\)

acf4c9d951e7af0b1be780d3813c0958ccafcb98.title: Conditional mean range
acf4c9d951e7af0b1be780d3813c0958ccafcb98.body:
For the potential outcomes in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}, the conditional potential-outcome mean \(\mu_x(a)\) satisfies
\[
\frac18\le \mu_x(a)\le \frac78
\qquad
\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X\text{ and }a\in[0,1].
\]

1159dba7f98ee2164973b49b1017625df2febf9d.title: Structural threshold schedules
1159dba7f98ee2164973b49b1017625df2febf9d.body:
For the random potential-outcome schedule in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}, let \(U\) denote the uniform-rank coordinate and \(\mu_X(a)\) the conditional potential-outcome mean at the realized stratum. With \(P\)-probability one,
\[
Y(a)=\mathbf 1\{U\le \mu_X(a)\}
\qquad
\text{simultaneously for every }a\in[0,1].
\]

2f8f22f7fde3591ebb0eb40fdd35f84350388a26.title: Realized outcome consistency
2f8f22f7fde3591ebb0eb40fdd35f84350388a26.body:
The realized outcome \(Y\) equals the potential outcome from \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space} evaluated at the latent dose \(A\):
\[
Y=Y(A)\qquad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]

afec58293becf93ddc2d111f9bac1fa15f30acee.title: Binary potential outcomes
afec58293becf93ddc2d111f9bac1fa15f30acee.body:
The potential outcomes in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space} satisfy
\[
P\{Y(a)\in\{0,1\}\}=1
\qquad
\text{for every }a\in[0,1].
\]

740ebbb881e6d9aab05a53fbccaae4eb77b6e837.title: Bounded potential outcomes
740ebbb881e6d9aab05a53fbccaae4eb77b6e837.body:
The potential outcomes in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space} satisfy
\[
P\{Y(a)\in[0,1]\}=1
\qquad
\text{for every }a\in[0,1].
\]

5040cda6490c80bb5abc9314a63d483100037e70.title: Bounded structural law class \(\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\)
5040cda6490c80bb5abc9314a63d483100037e70.body:
\(\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\) is the class of structural probability laws \(P\) of \((X,A,Z,Y(\cdot),Y)\), for fixed \((\beta,\kappa,\sigma)\), satisfying the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Stratum overlap.)} \cref{obj:ass:stratum-overlap}.
\item \textbf{(Latent support.)} \cref{obj:ass:latent-support}.
\item \textbf{(Conditional design.)} \cref{obj:ass:weak-design}.
\item \textbf{(Mean smoothness.)} \cref{obj:ass:holder-mean}.
\item \textbf{(Mean range.)} \cref{obj:ass:mean-range}.
\item \textbf{(Gaussian channel.)} \cref{obj:ass:gaussian-channel}.
\item \textbf{(Error independence.)} \cref{obj:ass:error-independence}.
\item \textbf{(Conditional unconfoundedness.)} \cref{obj:ass:conditional-unconfoundedness}.
\item \textbf{(Bounded potential outcomes.)} \cref{obj:ass:bounded-potential-outcomes}.
\item \textbf{(Consistency.)} \cref{obj:ass:consistency}.
\end{itemize}
The coordinate spaces are the declared measurable spaces, with the public potential-outcome path space specified in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}. The contaminated dose is
\[
W=A+\sigma Z,
\]
and \(\mu_x\) denotes the conditional potential-outcome mean function. Membership in \(\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\) is determined by the ten conditions above.

043fbd7201038981de8447190ac606108aa941c7.title: Minimax risk \(R_n(\sigma)\)
043fbd7201038981de8447190ac606108aa941c7.body:
\[
R_n(\sigma)
=
\inf_T\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}}
E_{Q_P^n}\bigl|T-\theta(P)\bigr|.
\]
Here \(\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\) is the structural model class, \(Q_P^n\) is the sample observed law induced by \(P\), and \(\theta(P)\) is the population causal mean at the prespecified latent dose. The infimum ranges over all measurable, possibly randomized estimators \(T\) based on the observed records \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), with potential-outcome schedules as in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}.

89ac2526096b5c58f85d4ffc822aedadf8b05660.title: Honest interval length \(H_n(\sigma)\)

3cb8c262d35c5309bd85905492b67425d28f02e7.title: Observed-law separation lower bound
3cb8c262d35c5309bd85905492b67425d28f02e7.body:
Under the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Structural model.)} The potential-outcome schedules and structural model class are those of \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space,obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Threshold outcomes.)} The binary potential outcomes and structural threshold representation satisfy \cref{obj:ass:binary-potential-outcomes,obj:ass:structural-threshold}.
\item \textbf{(Uniform independent rank.)} The rank satisfies \cref{obj:ass:rank-uniform,obj:ass:rank-treatment-independence}.
\item \textbf{(Observed sampling.)} Sampling and the induced observed experiment are as in \cref{obj:ass:iid,obj:def:observed-experiment}.
\end{itemize}
there exist constants \(c>0\) and \(n_0\) such that, for every \(n\ge n_0\) and \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), there are laws \(P_+,P_-\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\) with the same latent design and Bernoulli structural outcomes satisfying
\[
\bigl|\theta(P_+)-\theta(P_-)\bigr|
\ge c\rho_{n,\sigma},
\qquad
\operatorname{TV}\bigl(Q_{P_+}^n,Q_{P_-}^n\bigr)
\le \frac15,
\]
where \(\rho_{n,\sigma}\) is the localization scale raised to the mean-smoothness exponent.

The reference law \(P_\star\) and the perturbed laws \(P_\pm\) are product-seed threshold laws generated by the conditional means
\[
\mu_\star\equiv\frac12,
\qquad
\mu_\pm(a_0+t)=\frac12\pm\delta(t),
\]
where \(a_0\) is the evaluation dose and \(t\) is the latent-dose displacement from \(a_0\). In the direct regime, the perturbation is
\[
\delta(t)
=
\varepsilon h_0^\beta
\left(1-\left(\frac{t}{h_0}\right)^2\right)^2
\mathbf1\{|t|\le h_0\},
\]
where \(h_0\) is the perturbation bandwidth. In each inverse regime, with support radius \(\ell\), packet degree \(m\), and filtered Jacobi packet \(\psi_m\), the same threshold laws have
\[
h=\frac{\ell}{m},
\qquad
\delta(t)=\varepsilon h^\beta\psi_m(t/\ell),
\qquad
J=\lfloor c_pm\rfloor,
\]
where \(J\) is the cancelled-moment cutoff and \(c_p\) links packet degree to cancellation order. For \(\sigma>0\), the chi-squared divergence between the observed laws induced by \(P_\pm\) and \(P_\star\) satisfies
\[
\chi^2(P_\pm,P_\star)
\le
C\sigma^{-\kappa-1}h^{2\beta+2\kappa+2}
\sum_{j\ge J}\frac{(\ell^2/\sigma^2)^j}{j!}.
\]

fa8d2b8c89e7f69a99398b2ad0babfa382c1299e.title: Total estimator \(\widehat\theta\)
fa8d2b8c89e7f69a99398b2ad0babfa382c1299e.body:
The inputs are the observed records \(O_i=(X_i,W_i,Y_i)\), indexed by \(i=0,\ldots,n-1\), the public class constants \(K=(p_{\min},c_{\mathrm{lo}},c_{\mathrm{hi}})\), and the ordered dictionary \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\) with scores \(A_q(K)\) from \cref{obj:synth_4}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Form the sample blocks, their sizes, and the centered observed doses:
\[
\mathcal I_r
=\{i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}:i\bmod3=r\},
\qquad
N_r=|\mathcal I_r|,
\qquad r\in\{0,1,2\},
\]
\[
V_i=W_i-a_0,\qquad i=0,\ldots,n-1.
\]
\item If \(\min\{N_0,N_1,N_2\}=0\), output \(1/2\) and stop. The remaining steps apply when all three blocks are nonempty.
\item For each dictionary weight \(q\), use the public denominator bound
\[
I_\kappa(q)=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^\kappa q(t)\,dt,
\qquad
b_q(K)=p_{\min}c_{\mathrm{lo}}I_\kappa(q).
\]
Compute, for each stratum \(x\in\mathcal X=\{0,1\}\),
\[
\widehat p_x
=\frac1{N_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_0}\mathbf1\{X_i=x\},
\]
\[
\widehat D_x(q)
=\frac1{N_1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_1}
\mathbf1\{X_i=x\}\ell_q(V_i),
\qquad
\widehat M_x(q)
=\frac1{N_2}\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_2}
\mathbf1\{X_i=x\}Y_i\ell_q(V_i).
\]
\item Floor each denominator, project the ratio onto \([0,1]\) as in \cref{obj:synth_3}, and combine strata:
\[
\widehat\mu_x(q)
=\min\left\{1,\max\left\{0,
\frac{\widehat M_x(q)}
{\max\{\widehat D_x(q),b_q(K)/2\}}
\right\}\right\},
\qquad
\widehat\theta_q
=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat p_x\widehat\mu_x(q).
\]
\item Select the first public-score minimizer in the fixed dictionary order:
\[
\widehat q
=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{q\in\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}}A_q(K),
\]
with ties resolved by that order.
\item Output \(\widehat\theta=\widehat\theta_{\widehat q}\).
\end{enumerate}

3110fd1d294e438997bcda3e81bf91f0ba283f4b.title: Honest interval \(C_{n,\sigma}\)
3110fd1d294e438997bcda3e81bf91f0ba283f4b.body:
The connected interval is
\[
C_{n,\sigma}=
\begin{cases}
[\widehat\theta-10A_{\widehat q},
 \widehat\theta+10A_{\widehat q}]\cap[1/8,7/8],
& \mathcal I_r\ne\varnothing\ \text{for every }r\in\{0,1,2\},\\
[1/8,7/8],
& \mathcal I_r=\varnothing\ \text{for some }r\in\{0,1,2\}.
\end{cases}
\]
Here \(\mathcal I_r\) are the public modulo-three sample blocks, \(\widehat q\) is the first public-score minimizer in the fixed dictionary order, and \(\widehat\theta\) is the corresponding total estimator.

6df7c0d5e838777ad1722da572706519678cca35.title: Filtered Jacobi packet \(\psi_m\)
6df7c0d5e838777ad1722da572706519678cca35.body:
For each integer \(m\ge4\), the zero-extended filtered Jacobi packet is
\[
\psi_m(u)=
\begin{cases}
(1-u^2)^r K_m(2u^2-1)/K_m(-1),
& |u|\le1,\ \kappa>0,\\
(1-u^2)^r\widetilde K_m(u)/\widetilde K_m(0),
& |u|\le1,\ \kappa=0,\\
0,& |u|>1.
\end{cases}
\]
The fixed taper parameter and smooth spectral filter are
\[
r=4,\qquad
\eta(s)=
\begin{cases}
\exp\{-1/((s-9/8)(15/8-s))\},
& 9/8<s<15/8,\\
0,& \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
The filter is nonnegative, supported inside \((1,2)\), and positive on \([5/4,7/4]\). Write \(\mathsf J_j^{(a,b)}\) for the standard Jacobi polynomial of degree \(j\), and define its squared norm by
\[
H_j^{a,b}
=
\int_{-1}^{1}
\bigl(\mathsf J_j^{(a,b)}(z)\bigr)^2
(1-z)^a(1+z)^b\,dz.
\]
For \(\kappa>0\), the endpoint parameter and filtered sum are
\[
b=\frac{\kappa-1}{2},\qquad
K_m(z)=\sum_{j\ge0}\eta(j/m)
\frac{\mathsf J_j^{(r,b)}(-1)\mathsf J_j^{(r,b)}(z)}
{H_j^{r,b}}.
\]
For \(\kappa=0\), the symmetric interior sum is
\[
\widetilde K_m(u)=\sum_{j\ge0}\eta(j/m)
\frac{\mathsf J_j^{(r,r)}(0)\mathsf J_j^{(r,r)}(u)}
{H_j^{r,r}}.
\]

f2e72b11d2c2743df33b57d64228534cae5707d7.title: Potential-outcome space \((\mathcal S,\mathcal E)\)
f2e72b11d2c2743df33b57d64228534cae5707d7.body:
The public potential-outcome space \((\mathcal S,\mathcal E)\) is a measurable space of Borel functions from \([0,1]\) to \(\mathbb R\), satisfying the following conditions.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Evaluation.)} The evaluation map
\[
e:\mathcal S\times[0,1]\longrightarrow\mathbb R,
\qquad e(f,a)=f(a),
\]
is jointly measurable for the product sigma algebra \(\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal B([0,1])\).
\item \textbf{(Extensionality.)} For \(f,g\in\mathcal S\),
\[
f=g
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
e(f,a)=e(g,a)\ \text{for every }a\in[0,1].
\]
\item \textbf{(Threshold schedules.)} The space includes threshold schedules through the measurable map
\[
\iota:C([0,1],[0,1])\times[0,1]\longrightarrow\mathcal S,
\qquad
\iota(f,u)(a)=\mathbf1\{u\le f(a)\},
\]
where \(C([0,1],[0,1])\) carries its uniform-norm Borel sigma algebra.
\end{itemize}
The results apply to every fixed public space satisfying these conditions, with general schedules drawn from its Borel member functions. The potential-outcome schedule \(Y(\cdot)\) is a measurable random element of \(\mathcal S\), and its evaluation at dose \(a\) is
\[
Y(a)=e(Y(\cdot),a).
\]

e47959a9f2ce84bf773fa95520379961157f4e8c.title: Conditional potential mean \(\mu_x(a)\)
e47959a9f2ce84bf773fa95520379961157f4e8c.body:
The conditional potential-outcome mean is
\[
\mu_x(a)
=
E_P[Y(a)\mid X=x]
=
\frac{E_P[\mathbf1\{X=x\}Y(a)]}{p_x},
\qquad a\in[0,1],\quad x\in\mathcal X,\quad p_x>0.
\]
Here \(P\) is the structural probability law, \(X\) is the observed stratum coordinate, \(\mathcal X\) is the set of two observed strata, and
\[
p_x=P(X=x).
\]
The potential outcome \(Y(a)\) is the schedule evaluation in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}. Under the bounded-potential-outcome condition, the expectation exists and belongs to \([0,1]\). The model's stratum-overlap condition supplies \(p_x>0\) for both strata.

7000a7c32f34387062fb3795f87b1598856742db.title: Hölder increments and mean range
7000a7c32f34387062fb3795f87b1598856742db.body:
For the potential-outcome schedules in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}, let \(\mu_x\) denote the conditional potential-outcome mean function in stratum \(x\). For every observed stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), the radius-one Hölder class is defined by the increment seminorm:
\[
\mathcal H^\beta([0,1])
=
\left\{
f:[0,1]\to\mathbb R:
\sup_{\substack{a,a'\in[0,1]\\a\ne a'}}
\frac{|f(a)-f(a')|}{|a-a'|^\beta}\le1
\right\}.
\]
The mean satisfies
\[
\mu_x\in\mathcal H^\beta([0,1]),
\qquad
[\mu_x]_\beta
:=
\sup_{\substack{a,a'\in[0,1]\\a\ne a'}}
\frac{|\mu_x(a)-\mu_x(a')|}{|a-a'|^\beta}
\le1.
\]
Its range restriction is imposed separately:
\[
\mu_x(a)\in[1/8,7/8],
\qquad a\in[0,1].
\]

3a46359a623cef806026146678f3a1541f8c1939.title: Polynomial conditional design envelopes
3a46359a623cef806026146678f3a1541f8c1939.body:
For the structural law \(P\), let \(X\) be the observed coordinate taking values in the two-stratum space \(\mathcal X\), let \(A\) be the latent dose coordinate, and let \(a_0\) be the prespecified evaluation dose. For \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\), there exist measurable functions \(g_x:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\), indexed by \(x\in\mathcal X\), such that the image under \(A-a_0\) of the normalized restriction
\[
P(\{X=x\})^{-1}P|_{\{X=x\}}
\]
has Lebesgue density \(g_x\) on \([-1/2,1/2]\) and zero density outside this interval. For every \(x\in\mathcal X\),
\[
\frac14|t|^\kappa\le g_x(t)\le16|t|^\kappa
\]
for Lebesgue-almost every \(t\in[-1/2,1/2]\).

5997c9c2c449a080ac37b95f35dd9223e00203d8.title: Finite-sample honesty and length
5997c9c2c449a080ac37b95f35dd9223e00203d8.body:
Set the noncoverage probability to \(\alpha=1/10\). The guarantees below hold under the following conditions:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Smoothness parameter.)} \(\beta\in[1/2,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Design parameter.)} \(\kappa\in[0,2]\).
\item \textbf{(Potential-outcome space.)} The public measurable schedule space \((\mathcal S,\mathcal E)\) satisfies \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}.
\item \textbf{(Structural model.)} For each error scale \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), the structural law \(P\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\) as defined in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, carrying the restrictions in \cref{obj:ass:stratum-overlap,obj:ass:latent-support,obj:ass:weak-design,obj:ass:holder-mean,obj:ass:mean-range,obj:ass:gaussian-channel,obj:ass:error-independence,obj:ass:conditional-unconfoundedness,obj:ass:bounded-potential-outcomes,obj:ass:consistency}.
\end{itemize}
Define the population causal target by
\[
\theta(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y(a_0)],
\]
where \(a_0\) is the prespecified evaluation dose and \(Y(a_0)\) is the potential outcome at that dose. Let \(Q_P^n\) be the observed product experiment in \cref{obj:def:observed-experiment}, let \(C_{n,\sigma}\) be the interval in \cref{obj:def:honest-interval}, and let \(\rho_{n,\sigma}\) be the frontier rate in \cref{obj:def:frontier-rate}.

For every such schedule space, every integer \(n\ge0\), every \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), and every \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\),
\[
Q_P^n\{\theta(P)\in C_{n,\sigma}\}\ge 1-\alpha.
\]

af6e5aadc817c7073766e572e0a9ccf0a46a2b18.title: Observed-law lower-bound witnesses
af6e5aadc817c7073766e572e0a9ccf0a46a2b18.body:
Fix the mean-smoothness exponent \(\beta\in[1/2,1]\) and the design-decay exponent \(\kappa\in[0,2]\). There exist positive constants \(c,C,\varepsilon,C_{\mathrm{packet}},c_p\) and an integer \(n_0\), depending on \(\beta,\kappa\), with the following properties.

The filtered Jacobi packets \(\psi_m\) of \cref{obj:def:packet-handle} satisfy the packet guarantees of \cref{obj:thm:weighted-packet-construction} with constants \(C_{\mathrm{packet}},c_p\), uniformly over integers \(m\ge4\). In particular, their normalizing values satisfy
\[
\begin{cases}
K_m(-1)>0,&\kappa>0,\\
\widetilde K_m(0)>0,&\kappa=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Each zero-extended packet is even and continuously differentiable on \(\mathbb R\), and
\[
\psi_m(u)=0\quad (|u|>1),\qquad
\psi_m(0)=1,\qquad
|\psi_m(u)|\le C_{\mathrm{packet}},\qquad
|\psi_m'(u)|\le C_{\mathrm{packet}}m.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\int_{-1}^{1}|u|^\kappa|\psi_m(u)|\,du
\le C_{\mathrm{packet}}m^{-\kappa-1},
\qquad
\int_{-1}^{1}|u|^\kappa\psi_m(u)^2\,du
\le C_{\mathrm{packet}}m^{-\kappa-1},
\]
and, for every integer \(j\ge0\) with \(j<c_pm\),
\[
\int_{-1}^{1}|u|^\kappa u^j\psi_m(u)\,du=0.
\]

For every public measurable schedule space and potential-path structure as in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}, every \(n\ge n_0\), and every \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), there exist three structural probability laws \(P_+,P_-,P_\star\) with the following properties:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model membership.)} All three laws belong to \(\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\), the structural model class of \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Threshold outcomes.)} Each law satisfies \cref{obj:ass:binary-potential-outcomes,obj:ass:structural-threshold}.
\item \textbf{(Uniform independent rank.)} Under each law, the rank coordinate \(U\) satisfies \cref{obj:ass:rank-uniform,obj:ass:rank-treatment-independence}.
\item \textbf{(Observed sampling.)} Each law induces the independent observed sample and product experiment of \cref{obj:ass:iid,obj:def:observed-experiment}.
\item \textbf{(Common latent design.)} The observed stratum coordinate \(X\) and latent dose coordinate \(A\) have the same joint distribution under all three laws:
\[
\mathcal L_{P_+}(X,A)
=
\mathcal L_{P_-}(X,A)
=
\mathcal L_{P_\star}(X,A).
\]
\end{itemize}

\[

\le
|\theta(P_+)-\theta(P_-)|,
\qquad
\operatorname{TV}(Q_{P_+}^n,Q_{P_-}^n)\le\frac15,
\]
where \(\rho_{n,\sigma}\) is the frontier rate of \cref{obj:def:frontier-rate}.

ceeceb3fa8853fe55ff7aa918b1aef00ed0e99b4.title: Uniform risk and length frontier
ceeceb3fa8853fe55ff7aa918b1aef00ed0e99b4.body:
Fix the smoothness and design-decay exponents subject to:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Smoothness.)} \(\beta\in[1/2,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Design decay.)} \(\kappa\in[0,2]\).
\end{itemize}
Use the effective exponent \(d\), logarithmic sample scale \(L_n\), localization scale \(b_{n,\sigma}\), and risk frontier \(\rho_{n,\sigma}\) from \cref{obj:def:frontier-rate}, so that
\[
d=2\beta+\kappa+1,\qquad L_n=\log(en),\qquad
\rho_{n,\sigma}=b_{n,\sigma}^{\beta}.
\]
Define the transition thresholds \(a_n,b_n\) and comparison scales \(D_n,F_n,P_n\) by
\[
a_n=n^{-1/d},\qquad b_n=L_n^{-1/2},\qquad D_n=a_n,
\]
\[
F_n(\sigma)=\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{\log(e+n\sigma^d)}},
\qquad
P_n(\sigma)=\frac{\log(e+\sigma^2L_n)}{L_n}.
\]
For every public potential-outcome path space on any measurable schedule space as in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}, use \(R_n(\sigma)\), the randomized minimax expected absolute error, and \(H_n(\sigma)\), the minimum worst-law expected connected-interval length, from \cref{obj:def:minimax-risk,obj:def:honest-length}. Fix the noncoverage probability at
\[
\alpha=\frac{1}{10}.
\]

There exist real constants \(0<c<C\) and a natural number \(n_0\), uniform over all these path spaces, such that for every such path space, every natural number \(n\ge n_0\), and every \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\),
\[
c\rho_{n,\sigma}\le R_n(\sigma)\le C\rho_{n,\sigma},
\qquad
c\rho_{n,\sigma}\le H_n(\sigma)\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}.
\]
The same constant \(C\) satisfies, for every natural number \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
D_n\le C F_n(a_n),\qquad F_n(a_n)\le C D_n,
\]
\[
F_n(b_n)\le C P_n(b_n),\qquad
P_n(b_n)\le C F_n(b_n).
\]

For every real \(K\ge1\), there exist a real constant \(C_K\ge1\) and a natural number \(n_K\) such that for every natural number \(n\ge n_K\),
\[
0<\frac{a_n}{K},\qquad Ka_n\le\frac14,\qquad
0<\frac{b_n}{K},\qquad Kb_n\le\frac14.
\]
For every such \(n\), the same constant \(C_K\) gives both transition-window comparisons:
\[
C_K^{-1}D_n\le F_n(\sigma)\le C_KD_n
\qquad\text{for every }\sigma\in[a_n/K,Ka_n],
\]
\[
C_K^{-1}P_n(\sigma)\le F_n(\sigma)\le C_KP_n(\sigma)
\qquad\text{for every }\sigma\in[b_n/K,Kb_n].
\]

For every fixed \(\sigma\in(0,1/4]\), there exist real constants \(0<c_\sigma<C_\sigma\) and a natural number \(n_\sigma\), uniform over all the public path spaces, such that for every such path space and every natural number \(n\ge n_\sigma\),
\[
c_\sigma\left(\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^\beta
\le R_n(\sigma)\le
C_\sigma\left(\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^\beta,
\]
\[
c_\sigma\left(\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^\beta
\le H_n(\sigma)\le
C_\sigma\left(\frac{\log\log n}{\log n}\right)^\beta.
\]

e62b4f589e785b785ecddcd0e2c4d358f90dec09.title: Observable upper risk bound
e62b4f589e785b785ecddcd0e2c4d358f90dec09.body:
Fix the smoothness exponent \(\beta\in[1/2,1]\) and the design-decay exponent \(\kappa\in[0,2]\). There exist a constant \(C>0\) and an integer \(n_0\ge0\), uniform over all measurable potential-path spaces in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}, such that the following assertions hold for every such space, every integer \(n\ge n_0\), and every public error scale \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\).

Let \(\widehat\theta\) be the total estimator, including its empty-block fallback, in \cref{obj:def:total-estimator}, and let \(Q_P^n\) be the observed product experiment in \cref{obj:def:observed-experiment}. Write
\[
\theta(P)=E_P[Y(a_0)],
\]
where \(a_0\) is the prespecified evaluation dose. Let \(L_n=\log(en)\) and \(\rho_{n,\sigma}=b_{n,\sigma}^{\beta}\), with the localization scale \(b_{n,\sigma}\) defined in \cref{obj:def:frontier-rate}. For every structural law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\) as defined in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, under the sampling condition in \cref{obj:ass:iid},
\[
E_{Q_P^n}\!\left[|\widehat\theta-\theta(P)|\right]
\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}.
\]

The public dictionary \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\) in \cref{obj:def:weight-dictionary} also contains comparison pairs with the following guarantees. For a pair, write \(q\) for its latent weight, \(\ell_q\) for its observable inverse, and \(A_q\) for its public score in \cref{obj:def:weight-dictionary}. Define its weighted moment and extended inverse-weight second moment by
\[
I_\kappa(q)=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^\kappa q(t)\,dt,
\qquad
V_q=16\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^\kappa
E\!\left[\ell_q(t+\sigma Z)^2\right]\,dt,
\qquad Z\sim N(0,1),
\]
where the nonnegative second-moment integral may take the value \(+\infty\). Each comparison pair below satisfies the usual measurability and integrability conditions, together with
\[
q(t)\ge0\quad\text{for }t\in[-1/2,1/2],
\qquad
0<I_\kappa(q)<\infty,
\]
and the pointwise Gaussian inversion identity
\[
E\!\left[\ell_q(t+\sigma Z)\right]=q(t)
\quad\text{for every }t\in[-1/2,1/2].
\]
More precisely:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Fourier comparison.)}
If \(\sigma\le L_n^{-1/2}\), there exists an integer \(k\ge0\) whose Fourier tag belongs to \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\). The associated Fourier pair satisfies the conditions above and
\[
V_q<\infty,
\qquad A_q\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Polynomial comparison.)}
If \(L_n^{-1/2}<\sigma\), there exists an integer \(j\ge0\) whose polynomial tag belongs to \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\). The associated pair is
\[
(q,\ell_q)=\bigl(q_m^{\mathrm M},\ell_m^{\mathrm M}\bigr),
\qquad m=2^j+1,
\]
where \(m\) is the polynomial-family index. This pair satisfies the conditions above and
\[
V_q<\infty,
\qquad A_q\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}.
\]
\end{itemize}

7c9ab5b4d14afa1dd9741ab2f048936f0e3d5f1c.body:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class constants.)} \(0<p_{\min}\le 1/2\) and \(0<c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}\).
\item \textbf{(Smoothness.)} \(0<\beta\le 1\).
\item \textbf{(Design decay.)} \(0\le\kappa\le 2\).
\item \textbf{(Honesty level.)} \(0<\alpha<1\), where \(\alpha\) is the noncoverage probability.
\end{itemize}
For any public potential-outcome path space as in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}, let \(P\) range over the structural laws in \(\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\) with public constants \(K\). Write
\[
\theta(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y(a_0)],
\qquad
\rho_{n,\sigma}=b_{n,\sigma}^{\beta},
\]
where \(a_0\) is the prespecified latent evaluation dose and \(b_{n,\sigma}\) is the localization scale of the frontier construction. Let \(Q_P^n\) be the observed sample law in \cref{obj:def:observed-experiment}, and let \(C_{n,\sigma}\) be the interval in \cref{obj:def:honest-interval}, constructed with \(K,\beta,\kappa,\alpha\).

\[
Q_P^n\!\left\{\theta(P)\in C_{n,\sigma}\right\}\ge 1-\alpha.
\]

b8068e4de173c59c7f4ea03809361372f1803f77.title: Identification of the causal mean
b8068e4de173c59c7f4ea03809361372f1803f77.body:

Consider structural probability laws \(P\) and \(P'\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Parameter ranges.)} \(\beta\in(0,1]\), \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), and \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\).
\item \textbf{(Common model class.)} Both laws belong to the model class of \cref{obj:def:model-class} with the same \(K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma\) and public potential-path space.
\item \textbf{(Observed-law equality.)} Writing \(W=A+\sigma Z\) for the contaminated dose, the laws of the observed record coincide:
\[
\mathcal L_P(X,W,Y)=\mathcal L_{P'}(X,W,Y).
\]
\end{itemize}
For either structural law, write \(p_x(P)=P(X=x)\), and let \(\mu_x(a;P)\) denote its conditional potential-outcome mean from \cref{obj:def:conditional-potential-mean}. Set \(a_0=1/2\), the target dose, and \(t=A-a_0\), the centered latent dose. Define the population causal mean by
\[
\theta(P)=\int Y(a_0)\,dP,
\]
and analogously for \(P'\).

Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the stratum masses and conditional centered-dose measures agree:
\[
p_x(P)=p_x(P'),
\qquad
\mathcal L_P(A-a_0\mid X=x)
=
\mathcal L_{P'}(A-a_0\mid X=x).
\]
Their conditional latent mean measures also agree: for every Borel set \(B\subseteq\mathbb R\),
\[
\int_B \mu_x(t+a_0;P)\,
        \mathcal L_P(A-a_0\mid X=x)(dt)
=
\int_B \mu_x(t+a_0;P')\,
        \mathcal L_{P'}(A-a_0\mid X=x)(dt).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\mu_x(a;P)=\mu_x(a;P')
\qquad\text{for every }a\in[0,1].
\]
For every integer \(j\ge0\), the shrinking neighborhood has positive conditional latent mass:
\[
P\!\left(
-\frac1{j+3}<A-a_0<\frac1{j+3}
\,\middle|\,X=x
\right)>0,
\]
and its mean-measure to dose-measure ratio satisfies
\[
\lim_{j\to\infty}
\frac{
\displaystyle
\int_{(-1/(j+3),\,1/(j+3))}
\mu_x(t+a_0;P)\,
\mathcal L_P(A-a_0\mid X=x)(dt)
}{
\displaystyle
P\!\left(
-\frac1{j+3}<A-a_0<\frac1{j+3}
\,\middle|\,X=x
\right)
}
=
\mu_x(a_0;P).
\]
Finally,
\[
\theta(P)
=
\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_x(P)\mu_x(a_0;P),
\qquad
\theta(P)=\theta(P').
\]

45e5342eacccd6ee218806856167302a68ab0861.title: Dictionary admissibility and score rate
45e5342eacccd6ee218806856167302a68ab0861.body:
Fix the following public objects and parameters:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Path space.)} A potential-path space \((\mathcal S,\mathcal E)\) satisfying \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}.
\item \textbf{(Class constants.)} \(K=(p_{\min},c_{\mathrm{lo}},c_{\mathrm{hi}})\), with
\[
0<p_{\min}\le \tfrac12,
\qquad
0<c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Exponents.)} \(\beta\in(0,1]\) and \(\kappa\in[0,2]\).
\end{itemize}
Use the public dictionary of inverse pairs and scores in \cref{obj:def:weight-dictionary}. For every integer \(n\ge1\), every \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), and every pair \((q,\ell_q)\in\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\), the weights are measurable, \(q(t)\ge0\) on \([-1/2,1/2]\), and
\[
0<
\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^\kappa q(t)\,dt
<\infty.
\]
For every \(t\in[-1/2,1/2]\), the Gaussian inverse is absolutely integrable and satisfies
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}|\ell_q(t+\sigma z)|\,d\Phi_1(z)<\infty,
\qquad
\int_{\mathbb R}\ell_q(t+\sigma z)\,d\Phi_1(z)=q(t),
\]
where \(\Phi_1\) is the standard Gaussian probability measure. Its public inverse-weight second moment is finite:
\[
V_q
=
16\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^\kappa
\left(\int_{\mathbb R}\ell_q(t+\sigma z)^2\,d\Phi_1(z)\right)\,dt
<\infty.
\]
Moreover, under every structural law \(P\in\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\), the inverse weight evaluated at the observed centered dose \(V\) is absolutely integrable:
\[
\mathbb E_P\!\left[|\ell_q(V)|\right]<\infty.
\]

Let \(\widehat q\) be the first minimizer, in the fixed dictionary order, of the public score:
\[
\widehat q
=
\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{q\in\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}} A_q(K).
\]
Write \(\rho_{n,\sigma}=b_{n,\sigma}^{\beta}\) for the frontier rate, where \(b_{n,\sigma}\) is the localization scale, and \(L_n\) for the logarithmic sample-size quantity. There exist \(C>0\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), depending on the fixed public parameters and uniformly valid over \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\), such that, for every \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
A_{\widehat q}(K)\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}.
\]
If \(\sigma\le L_n^{-1/2}\), there is a Fourier dictionary index \(k\in\mathbb N\) whose associated pair belongs to \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\) and whose score is at most \(C\rho_{n,\sigma}\). If \(L_n^{-1/2}<\sigma\), there is \(j\in\mathbb N\) such that the polynomial inverse pair with index \(m=2^j+1\) belongs to \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\) and satisfies
\[
A_{q_m^{\mathrm M}}(K)\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}.
\]

a2fbb552cb0e26861ffe7bab60073beab34c84b8.title: Observable absolute-error upper bound
a2fbb552cb0e26861ffe7bab60073beab34c84b8.body:
Fix the following public parameters:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class constants.)} \(K\) specifies a minimum stratum mass in \((0,1/2]\) and positive lower and upper weak-design envelope constants, with the lower constant at most the upper constant.
\item \textbf{(Smoothness.)} The smoothness exponent satisfies \(\beta\in(0,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Design decay.)} The design-decay exponent satisfies \(\kappa\in[0,2]\).
\end{itemize}
There exist \(C>0\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), depending on \(K,\beta,\kappa\), such that the following guarantees hold uniformly over every measurable schedule space and potential-path structure in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}, every \(n\ge n_0\), and every public error scale \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\). Write
\[
L_n=\log(en),
\qquad
\rho_{n,\sigma}=b_{n,\sigma}^{\beta},
\]
where \(b_{n,\sigma}\) is the frontier localization scale.

For every structural probability law \(P\) satisfying the bounded noisy-dose model restrictions with parameters \(K,\beta,\kappa,\sigma\), under the sampling condition in \cref{obj:ass:iid}, the observed experiment \(Q_P^n\) in \cref{obj:def:observed-experiment} and the selected estimator \(\widehat\theta\) in \cref{obj:def:total-estimator} satisfy
\[
\mathbb E_{Q_P^n}\!\left[
  \left|\widehat\theta-\theta(P)\right|
\right]
\le C\rho_{n,\sigma},
\qquad
\theta(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y(a_0)],
\]
where \(a_0\) is the prespecified evaluation dose and \(Y(a_0)\) is the potential outcome obtained by evaluating the random schedule there.

The public dictionary \(\mathcal D_{n,\sigma}\) in \cref{obj:def:weight-dictionary} also contains comparison witnesses with the following guarantees:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Fourier range.)} If \(\sigma\le L_n^{-1/2}\), there is a Fourier dictionary entry, indexed by a nonnegative integer, whose associated pair \((q_h^{\mathrm F},\ell_h^{\mathrm F})\) has public expected-error score
\[
A_{q_h^{\mathrm F}}\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Polynomial range.)} If \(L_n^{-1/2}<\sigma\), there is a polynomial dictionary entry, indexed by a nonnegative integer, whose associated pair \((q_m^{\mathrm M},\ell_m^{\mathrm M})\) has public expected-error score
\[
A_{q_m^{\mathrm M}}\le C\rho_{n,\sigma}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Here the pairs and their public scores are those associated with the entries of \cref{obj:def:weight-dictionary}. Each witness pair \((q,\ell_q)\) satisfies, under the usual measurability and integrability conditions,
\[
q(t)\ge0
\quad\text{for every }t\in[-1/2,1/2],
\qquad
0<I_\kappa(q)
:=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^\kappa q(t)\,dt<\infty,
\qquad
V_q<\infty,
\]
where \(V_q\) is its public second-moment bound, and its Gaussian inversion identity holds pointwise:
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}\ell_q(t+\sigma z)
       \frac{e^{-z^2/2}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\,dz
=q(t)
\quad\text{for every }t\in[-1/2,1/2].
\]

4364aec7ffb9037ec5dd7fefaf145b35d81a1d2d.title: Positive denominators and approximation
4364aec7ffb9037ec5dd7fefaf145b35d81a1d2d.body:
Fix a potential-path space \((\mathcal S,\mathcal E)\) as in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}. Let \(\mathcal X\) consist of two strata, and let \(P\) be a structural probability law with coordinates \(X\in\mathcal X\), \(A,Z,Y,U\in\mathbb R\), and potential-outcome schedule \(Y(\cdot)\in\mathcal S\). Set
\[
a_0=\frac12,\qquad t=A-a_0,\qquad W=A+\sigma Z,\qquad V=W-a_0=t+\sigma Z.
\]
Let \(q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be a public latent weight and \(\ell_q:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) its observable inverse weight. Define the weighted moments by
\[
I_\gamma(q)=\int_{-1/2}^{1/2}|t|^\gamma q(t)\,dt.
\]
Suppose the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Public constants.)} The constants \(K=(p_{\min},c_{\mathrm{lo}},c_{\mathrm{hi}})\) satisfy
\[
0<p_{\min}\le\frac12,\qquad 0<c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Parameter ranges.)}
\[
\beta\in(0,1],\qquad \kappa\in[0,2],\qquad \sigma\in[0,1/4].
\]
\item \textbf{(Structural model.)} The law \(P\) satisfies \cref{obj:def:model-class} with path space \((\mathcal S,\mathcal E)\), constants \(K\), and parameters \((\beta,\kappa,\sigma)\).
\item \textbf{(Admissible weight.)} The functions \(q\) and \(\ell_q\) are measurable, and
\[
q(t)\ge0\quad\text{for every }t\in[-1/2,1/2],
\qquad 0<I_\kappa(q)<\infty.
\]
\item \textbf{(Exact Gaussian inversion.)} For every \(t\in[-1/2,1/2]\), the function \(z\mapsto\ell_q(t+\sigma z)\) is absolutely integrable under the standard Gaussian law, and
\[
\int_{\mathbb R}\ell_q(t+\sigma z)\frac{e^{-z^2/2}}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\,dz=q(t).
\]
The inverse weight is also absolutely integrable under the structural law:
\[
E_P[|\ell_q(V)|]<\infty.
\]
\end{itemize}
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the denominator is strictly positive and satisfies
\[
0<E_P[\mathbf1\{X=x\}\ell_q(V)],
\qquad
E_P[\mathbf1\{X=x\}\ell_q(V)]
\ge p_{\min}c_{\mathrm{lo}}I_\kappa(q).
\]
Consequently, the localized population ratio
\[
m_{x,q}
=
\frac{E_P[\mathbf1\{X=x\}Y\ell_q(V)]}
     {E_P[\mathbf1\{X=x\}\ell_q(V)]}
\]
is well defined and, with \(\mu_x(a_0)\) as in \cref{obj:def:conditional-potential-mean}, obeys
\[
|m_{x,q}-\mu_x(a_0)|
\le
\frac{c_{\mathrm{hi}}}{c_{\mathrm{lo}}}
\frac{I_{\kappa+\beta}(q)}{I_\kappa(q)}.
\]
These conclusions hold throughout the stated parameter ranges, including \(\sigma=0\).

89e95f907e9754ff34b394afa66dc9a90e5927e9.title: Realized dose conditional means
89e95f907e9754ff34b394afa66dc9a90e5927e9.body:
Suppose the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Public model primitives.)} Fix a potential-outcome path space as in \cref{obj:def:potential-path-space} and public class constants \(K\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}.
\item \textbf{(Parameter ranges.)} Let \(\beta\in(0,1]\), \(\kappa\in[0,2]\), and \(\sigma\in[0,1/4]\).
\item \textbf{(Structural law.)} Let \(P\) be a structural probability law in the model class \(\mathcal P_{\beta,\kappa,\sigma}\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with public constants \(K\). Write \(\mathcal X=\{0,1\}\) for the stratum space, and let \(X\in\mathcal X\), \(A\in\mathbb R\), \(Z\in\mathbb R\), and \(Y\in\mathbb R\) denote its stratum, latent dose, classical error, and realized outcome coordinates, respectively.
\end{itemize}
With \(\mu_x(a)\) denoting the conditional potential-outcome mean defined in \cref{obj:def:conditional-potential-mean}, the following statements hold \(P\)-almost surely:
\[
0\le Y\le1,\qquad
E_P[Y\mid A,X,Z]=\mu_X(A),\qquad
E_P[Y\mid A,X]=\mu_X(A).
\]
Moreover, for every bounded measurable function
\(F:\mathbb R\times\mathcal X\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\),
\[
E_P\!\left[F(A,X,Z)Y\right]
=
E_P\!\left[F(A,X,Z)\mu_X(A)\right].
\]

67b70c18ae05c261fb97b49142b11f5a9235a5ba.title: Error-free rates and benchmark comparison
67b70c18ae05c261fb97b49142b11f5a9235a5ba.body:
Fix the public class constants \(K=(p_{\min},c_{\mathrm{lo}},c_{\mathrm{hi}})\) and parameters \(\beta,\kappa,\alpha\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Class constants.)} \(0<p_{\min}\le 1/2\) and \(0<c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}\).
\item \textbf{(Parameter ranges.)} \(0<\beta\le1\), \(0\le\kappa\le2\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\), where \(\alpha\) is the noncoverage probability.
\item \textbf{(Envelope calibration.)}
\[
c_{\mathrm{lo}}\le(\kappa+1)2^\kappa\le c_{\mathrm{hi}}.
\]
\end{itemize}
There exist constants \(0<c<C\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\) such that, for every public potential-path space \((\mathcal S,\mathcal E)\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}\) and every integer \(n\ge n_0\), the minimax absolute risk and minimum honest expected connected-interval length of \(\cref{obj:def:minimax-risk,obj:def:honest-length}\) satisfy
\[
c\,n^{-\beta/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}
\le R_n(0)\le
C\,n^{-\beta/(2\beta+\kappa+1)},
\qquad
c\,n^{-\beta/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}
\le H_n(0)\le
C\,n^{-\beta/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}.
\]

Moreover, fix any separate direct Gaussian-response benchmark with:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Benchmark constants.)} \(c_{\mathrm G},r_{\mathrm G},M_{\mathrm G},\tau_{\mathrm G}>0\).
\item \textbf{(Evaluation neighborhood.)} \(x_*\in(0,1)\) and \(0<\delta\le\min\{x_*,1-x_*\}\).
\item \textbf{(Design.)} A fixed probability distribution \(\nu\) on \([0,1]\) with a nonnegative density \(g\) satisfying
\[
g(u)=c_{\mathrm G}|u-x_*|^\kappa
\quad\text{for }u\in[0,1]\text{ with }|u-x_*|\le\delta.
\]
\end{itemize}
The benchmark observations are \(B_i=f(D_i)+\xi_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), where the \(D_i\) are independent draws from \(\nu\), and the \(\xi_i\) are independent \(N(0,\tau_{\mathrm G}^2)\) errors independent of the design. In the supremum below, \(f\) ranges over Borel functions on \([0,1]\) satisfying
\[
\|f\|_\infty\le M_{\mathrm G},
\qquad
\inf_{\substack{p\text{ a real polynomial}\\ \deg p\le\lfloor\beta\rfloor}}
\ \sup_{\substack{u\in[0,1]\\ |u-x_*|\le a}}
|f(u)-p(u-x_*)|
\le r_{\mathrm G}a^\beta
\]
for every
\[
0<a\le
\left\{\frac{\tau_{\mathrm G}^2(\kappa+1)}
{2c_{\mathrm G}r_{\mathrm G}^2n}\right\}^{1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}.
\]
The infimum below ranges over measurable estimators from the benchmark observations, and \(E_f\) denotes expectation under their observed law. There exist constants \(0<c<C\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), now also depending on the fixed benchmark, such that for every public potential-path space satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:potential-path-space}\) and every integer \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
c\,\inf_{\widehat f}\sup_f E_f|\widehat f(x_*)-f(x_*)|
\le R_n(0)\le
C\,\inf_{\widehat f}\sup_f E_f|\widehat f(x_*)-f(x_*)|.
\]
